methodology: Independently read the pinned CSV and manifest, selected Darwin rows using the stated sorting-date or explicit-year rule, parsed all 476 preserved TEI XML files with a separate Python verifier, expanded every sent date constraint to inclusive bounds, classified records only when every possible sent date was inside the period, checked XML identity/topology/authority keys, recomputed hashes and correspondent counts, and compared the resulting record-level values with the supplied audit outputs.

checks.evidence: Independent selection produced 476 Darwin candidates and 13 in-window third-party exclusions.
All 476 manifest files exist, hashes match, XML root IDs match CSV IDs, and all 476 have one sent and one received action.
All selected rows matched the XML Darwin authority identity on the corresponding side.
Independent bounds expansion reproduced 445 safe and 31 held records and all four date-structure totals.
Independent XML action authority produced safe 318 outgoing/127 incoming and held 27 outgoing/4 incoming.
97 safe records require review because of non-single-day structure or textual date qualifiers.
DCP-LETT-512 has sent subtype personGrp with Darwin, C. R. and Darwin, Emma; it is the sole safe outgoing multi-sender record.
Recomputed authority-key counts match reports/1837-1843/correspondents.json, including Emma 18/14, Henslow 24/10, Kemp 11/6, and Lyell 17/5.
All 476 recomputed IDs and classification/direction fields match audit.jsonl.

date_and_boundary_findings.interpretation: Sorting dates are selection keys and do not resolve bounded ranges, alternatives, or textual qualifiers. Held records are boundary-ambiguous under the stated all-possibilities rule, not false eligibility determinations. DCP-LETT-326 is also the single supplemental candidate whose sorting date lies outside the period while its explicit range reaches into it.

limitations: The candidate set is a Darwin-only CSV sorting-date window plus explicit display-date years, not an XML-wide search of all 15,238 catalogue rows.

The 476-file metadata audit does not establish transcriptions, receipt dates, replies, individual prose authorship, or voice eligibility. The one joint-author record (512) remains held for authorship review.
The 445 safe records include 97 that still need exact chronological ordering review. Safe eligibility means all encoded possibilities fall inside the period; it does not make a sorting date exact.
The top correspondent counts are authority-key inventory counts, with joint correspondence counted by its combined participant set and historical labels retained.
verdict: The reported metadata findings are independently reproduced and supported. No record-level, hash, identity, date-classification, direction, completeness-within-selection, or correspondent-count error was found. The scope and chronology limitations above remain material.
